name: Three Card Monte
description: Three Card Monte is not a true game but a confidence trick: the dealer shows three cards (one is the queen), throws them face-down, and the punter bets on which is the queen. The dealer uses sleight of hand so the punter loses. Known as Find the Lady in Britain and Bonneteau in France.

rules.objective: Correctly identify which of the three face-down cards is the queen (or money card). In honest play between friends, the punter wins the stake back plus the same amount again for a correct guess; in the street scam the dealer uses sleight of hand so the punter loses.
rules.gameplay:
1. The dealer shows three cards (one queen, two others—often two black jacks).
2. The dealer throws the three cards face-down on the table and mixes them quickly.
3. The punter bets on which face-down card is the queen.
4. If correct (in honest play), the punter receives the stake back plus the same amount again; otherwise the stake is lost. In the scam, the dealer ensures the punter never wins.
keyRules: Only three cards are used: one target card (usually a queen) and two others.
The dealer mixes the cards face-down; the punter must track or guess the target card.
Bet is placed on one of the three positions before the chosen card is revealed.

strategy.basic: Do not play for money in street settings—it is a scam; the dealer uses sleight of hand and accomplices (shills) so the punter cannot win.
strategy.intermediate: If playing honestly with friends with no real money, the only skill is visual tracking of the queen during the mix; the dealer can make this very difficult.
strategy.advanced: Sources advise: play only with no real money involved and explain the trick afterwards. In a true monte scam the mark has no chance of winning.
tips: Do not be misled by apparent winners—they are often shills.
Play only for fun with friends and no money at stake.
